Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.behavior

Class ServerBehaviorScheduler

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.behavior.ServerBehaviorScheduler
public final class ServerBehaviorScheduler extends Object
The single authority for which eye behavior a mob is playing, and when. Behaviors are cosmetic and client-rendered, but the schedule is server-owned so the "one at a time, non-interruptable" rule holds across every viewer and so server-only game events drive the same path. Triggers are the ambient idle timer below plus game-event reactions (hurt → grow, trade/heal → swirl).

Server-polite: only mobs currently tracked by a player are considered — the tracked set is maintained from StartTracking/StopTracking (so we never scan all loaded entities). A tracked mob always gets a STATES entry (needed for the trackers count regardless of eye state), but serverTick() only walks ACTIVE, the subset that can actually do something: mobs known to have eyes, plus any mob mid-behavior (started via start(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity, com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.behavior.ServerBehaviorScheduler.MobState, com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.behavior.EyeBehavior, int, long), including the debug trigger(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity, com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.behavior.EyeBehavior, int, long)). A tracked-but-eyeless mob — the overwhelming majority, since the default spawn chance is 5% — costs one map entry and nothing per tick. onEyesGained(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity) promotes a mob into ACTIVE the moment its eyes turn on (natural spawn already tracked, or a mid-life slimy eye / admin toggle), called from EyeState. Once promoted, a mob stays in ACTIVE for the rest of its tracked lifetime even if it later loses its eyes again (shears) — simpler and safe (no risk of evicting a mob whose behavior still needs retiring), at the cost of walking a mob that transiently had eyes and lost them again while still tracked, which is rare enough not to matter.

State is per (integrated-or-dedicated) server lifetime; clear() is called on server stop so a single-player JVM doesn't carry one world's mobs into the next.

    • clear

      public static void clear()
      Forget all state (server stop), so a single-player JVM doesn't bleed one world into the next.

    • onEyesGained

      public static void onEyesGained(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity mob)
      Promote mob into the per-tick-walked ACTIVE set now that it's known to have eyes. A no-op if nobody is currently tracking it (no ServerBehaviorScheduler.MobState to promote) — onStartTracking(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer) independently checks EyeState.hasEyes(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity) for that case. Called from EyeState wherever the persisted has-eyes flag turns on.

    • onHealed

      public static void onHealed(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity mob)
      mob was healed: play 'swirl' (if enabled), rate-limited per mob so regen doesn't loop it.

    • onPlayerHurt

      public static void onPlayerHurt(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity mob)

    • onStartTracking

      public static void onStartTracking(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity mob, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player)
      A player started tracking mob. Always creates a STATES entry (needed for the trackers count regardless of eye state) and promotes into ACTIVE immediately if the mob already has eyes; a mid-life gain while already tracked comes through onEyesGained(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity) instead. Also catches the player up if the mob is already mid-effect.

    • onStopTracking

      public static void onStopTracking(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity mob)
      A player stopped tracking mob (including on its death/unload). Drops state when unwatched.

    • onTrade

      public static void onTrade(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity villager)
      villager completed a trade with a player: play 'swirl' (if enabled).

    • serverTick

      public static void serverTick()
      Advance the scheduler one server tick: retire finished behaviors, drop states for removed or unwatched-and-idle mobs, and roll a fresh ambient behavior when a watched eyed mob's cooldown expires. Walks only ACTIVE — see the class doc — so an eyeless tracked mob costs nothing per tick; a mob evicted here is dropped from STATES too, keeping the two in sync.

    • trigger

      public static boolean trigger(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity mob, EyeBehavior behavior, int duration, long seed)
      Try to start behavior on mob now, honoring "one at a time, non-interruptable": dropped (returns false) if the mob is already mid-behavior. Works even for a mob with no tracking state yet (creates one), so the debug command can drive any looked-at mob.
